title: The Violin Through the Wall
script: Ratna: [carefully diplomatic] Galih, I want to raise this before it calcifies into the sort of grievance that ambushes us during an unrelated argument three weeks from now.
Galih: [bracing] That's an ominous preamble. Is this about the practising?
Ratna: [candid] It is, though I want to be precise about the complaint, because I suspect a vague one will land as an accusation rather than a request.
Galih: [wary] Go on, then. I'd rather precision than a grudge left to fester.
Ratna: [measured] It's not the violin itself, which I genuinely enjoy hearing. It's that the scales arrive precisely when I'm on a client call, as though the two schedules were engineered to collide.
Galih: [defensive, softening] I hadn't clocked the overlap, honestly. I practise when I have energy for it, which tends to be late afternoon, same as your calls apparently.
Ratna: [gentler] I believe you. I'm not accusing you of sabotage, only of an oversight that's costing me something you can't easily see from your side of the wall.
Galih: [reflective] That's a fair distinction. It's easy to assume a closed door means the sound simply vanishes on the other side of it.
Ratna: [wry] It does not vanish. Your scales have become, unbidden, the soundtrack to several fairly important negotiations.
Galih: [amused despite himself] I'm almost flattered my mediocre technique has been so audible to strangers on the internet.
Ratna: [laughing] Audible and, on one memorable occasion, mistaken by a client for hold music.
Galih: [conceding] Right, that settles it. Let me shift practice to mornings before you're up, or evenings once you've finished for the day.
Ratna: [warm] Either works. I'd rather adapt around a fixed slot than have you constantly second-guessing when it's safe to pick up the bow.
Galih: [thoughtful] I'll aim for early mornings, actually. There's something almost monastic about scales before the flat's properly woken up.
Ratna: [smiling] I can live with monastic. I draw the line only at the concerto you've been murdering for a month.
Galih: [laughing] The concerto stays confidential until it's presentable. You have my word, and my considerable embarrassment, as collateral.

quiz.question: Why does Ratna say she wants to raise the issue precisely rather than vaguely?
options: She wants to end the friendship
A vague complaint might land as an accusation rather than a request
She enjoys confrontation
Galih asked her to be specific
quiz.explanation: Ratna explains that precision prevents the complaint from being misread as an accusation.

quiz.question: What is Ratna's actual complaint about the violin practice?
options: She dislikes the sound of the violin entirely
The scales coincide with her client calls, as if the schedules were engineered to collide
Galih plays too loudly at night
She wants him to stop playing altogether
quiz.explanation: Her complaint is about timing, not the music itself — the practice overlaps with her important calls.

quiz.question: What amusing detail does Ratna reveal about the violin's audibility?
options: Neighbors filed a complaint
A client once mistook the scales for hold music
The violin broke a window
Galih recorded it accidentally
quiz.explanation: Ratna mentions a client mistook Galih's scales for hold music during a call.

quiz.question: What solution does Galih propose?
options: Stopping the violin entirely
Shifting practice to early mornings before Ratna is up, or evenings after her workday
Moving out of the flat
Practicing only on weekends
quiz.explanation: Galih offers to move his practice sessions to early morning or evening to avoid the overlap.

quiz.question: What does Ratna say she draws the line at?
options: Any music practice at all
The concerto Galih has been struggling with for a month, until it's presentable
Practicing in the living room
Playing without headphones
quiz.explanation: Ratna jokes that she only objects to the unfinished concerto Galih has been struggling with.
